Rectors of
the College:

ST.
Patrick’s College has always had an illustrious line of Rectors. We recollect with gratitude the Rectors, both
foreign and native who made immense sacrifice to give form, character and
beauty to the magnificent structure it has now assumed.

Mr. Patrick
Foy (1850 – 1858)

Rev. Bro.
John Joseph Brown, OMI (1859 – 1861)

Rev. Fr.
Patrick Joseph Conway, OMI (1862 – 1870)

Rev. Fr.
Michael A. Murphy, OMI (1870)

Rev. Fr. P.
O’Flanangan, OMI (1870 – 1874; 1875 – 1880)

T.W. Mc
Mahan Esqr. (1874 – 1875)

Rev. Bro. (Fr.)
J. A. R. Smythe, OMI (1880 – 1883)

Rev. Fr.
Charles H. Lytton, OMI (1883 – 1885)

Rev. Fr.
Jules Collin, OMI (1885 – 1888; 1901 – 1902)

Rev. Fr. M.
Dubreuil, OMI (1888 – 1889)

Rev. Fr.
Patrick Dunne, OMI (1890 -1901)

Rev. Fr.
Charles A. Beaud, OMI (1902 – 1905)

Rev. Fr.
Charles S. Matthews, OMI (1905 – 1921; 1924 – 1936)

Rev. Fr.
John A. Guymar, OMI (1921 – 1924)

Rev. Fr.
Timothy M. F. Long, OMI (1936 – 1954)

Rev. Fr. S.
N. Arulnesan, OMI (1954 – 1960)

Rev. Fr. P.
J. Jeevaratnam, OMI (1960 – 1966)

Rev. Fr. T.
A. J. Mathuranayagam, (1966 – 1976)

Rev. Fr.
John A. Francis, OMI (1976 – 1979)

Rev. Fr. G.
A. Francis Joseph (1979 – 1992)

Rev. Fr. A.
I Bernard (1992 – 2002)

Rev. Fr.
Justin B. Gnanapragasam (2002 – 2007)

Rev. Fr. M.
Jero Selvanayagam (2007 – 2018)

Rev. Fr. A.
P. Thirumahan (2018 – to date)

Mr. Patrick
Foy (1850 – 1858)

When the
school was founded, it was the only Catholic English School for boys in the
north at that time. Its first Principal was Mr. Patrick Foy, an Irishman.

Rev. Fr.
Patrick J. Conway, OMI (1862 – 1869)

With the
Principalship of Rev.Fr. Patrick J. Conway there was a noticeable change in the
school. A more rounded education was
envisaged and the school had reached a really high standard. He died in February 1869. It was a day of mourning for the school.

Rev. Fr.
Michael A. Murphy, OMI (1870)

In 1867, Fr.
Murphy joined the staff of the College and acted for a short time as Principal
after the death of Fr. Conway. He led a
campaign to collect funds for erecting more buildings for the school. He took an interest in the varied activities
in Jaffna at that time. He was easily
accessible to everyone. When the deadly epidemic of cholera spread in Jaffna in
1876, Fr. Murphy attended the needs of the victims with great kindness. One of the finest memories that one keeps of
the early days is the College anthem, written by Fr. Murphy OMI. Generations of Patricians would remember Fr.
Murphy for the proud salutations of the College he gave them.Fr. Murphy was called to rest in January
1887.

Rev. Fr. P.
O’Flanangan, OMI (1870 – 1874; 1875 – 1880)

Bro.
Flanangan was the first old boy to become Principal of the School. He was one among the first batch of students
to be enrolled at the Jaffna Boys’ School. As a boy, his mischievous traits knew no bounds. Fr. Flanangan excelled in stage debates on
religious issues and was an eloquent preacher in Tamil too. After his retirement as Rector, he continues
to be the Manager of the school till his death. His whole life was devoted to the upliftment of the school in every
sphere of its activities. He died on 28th
January 1889.

Rev. Bro.
(Fr.) J. A. R. Smythe, OMI (1881 – 1883)

In response
to persistent demand from the Catholics of Jaffna for higher education
facilities, the College under its present name ST. PARITICK’S COLLEGE was
founded on the 10th of January 1881 and Rev. Fr. J.A. Smythe was the
first Rector of the new St. Patrick’s College. In matters of administration he showed sound judgment. His ready support and precious advice were
much sought after. He died in 1888. His death was mourned with a deep sense of
personal loss to all.

Rev. Fr.
Charles H. Lytton, OMI (1883 – 1885)

Rev. Fr.
Charles Lytton came to St. Patrick’s College to take up the position of Rector
in 1883. He took an interest in the
varied activities of the College. He loved
the Sacred Heart and his sincere devotion and faithfulness was paramount in is
life. In 1883 the “Prize – Giving” was
held in the College, for the first time. He was greatly missed when he left the College for parish work, only two
years after he arrived.

Rev. Fr.
Jules Collin, OMI (1885 – 1888; 1901 – 1902)

Fr. Jules
Collin succeeded Fr. Lytton. Through the
generosity of Bishop Melizan, 87 acres of land was received by the
College. The bishop also donated a
lustrous brass band which consisted of seventeen instruments costing Rs. 900, a
substantial sum then. It was used in all
school functions and was also played at public festivals. People came to the College to enjoy the rich
music offered by the band.

Rev. Fr. M.
Dubreuil, OMI (1888 – 1889)

Health
compelled Fr. Collin initially to relinquish his duties and Fr. Dubreuil took
over the reins as Rector for a year till Fr. Patrick Dunne was appointed in
1890.

Rev. Fr.
Patrick Dunne, OMI (1890 -1901)

During his
period, the number on roll expanded and the College became one of the leading
schools in the island. Students from all
parts of the country, were attracted to the portals of St. Patrick’s. His superiority in administrative capability
was solely due to his astuteness in judging people. Favouritism was not in him, nor did tell-tale
gain his attention. In 190r, Fr. Dunne
relinquished the post of Principal and left Jaffna. With him and the golden jubilee of St.
Patrick’s marked an end of the fifty years era in the history of our College.

Rev. Fr.
Charles A. Beaud, OMI (1902 – 1905)

Rev. Fr.
Charles succeeded Fr. Patrick Dunne in 1901. During the short period of his office, he make new additions to the
College buildings. He possessed a sound
knowledge of architecture which was a blessing for the College enabling us to
get a new set of classrooms and a study hall for the boarders. At this time foundation were laid for a new
secondary school and a laboratory.
Rev. Fr. Charles S. Matthews, OMI (1905 – 1921; 1924 – 1936)

Rev. Fr. Charles Matthews, a Canadian University graduate
had taught at St. Patrick’s for three years before succeeding Fr. Beaud as
Rector in 1906. He remained in office
till 1936 except for a break of short period and was indeed the chief architect
of St. Patrick’s, having served the longest period. The achievements of the school during his
time are too numerous to mention. He
organized the College and introduced rules and regulations. Studies and games were systemized and became
popular. At this time, the London
Matriculation examination results, secured for three years by St. Patrick’s
were the best in the British Empire. During his time 50% of the present Matthews block had been completed.

The statue of Our Lady of the Patricians was installed in
the College quadrangle by Fr. Matthews and it is a reflection of his great love
of the Mother of God which he infused in the hearts and minds of young
Patricians. In the long history of this
edifice, Fr. Matthews will rank as one of those Rectors who patiently and
perseveringly built on the existing traditions establishing his successes.
Rev. Fr. John A. Guymar, OMI (1921 – 1924)

Rev. Fr. Guyomar, a polished product of the University of
Cambridge, was sent to join St. Patrick’s as a young graduate in 1921. This young scholarly priest well-versed in
the Western Classics had the distinction of having won double first class in
the Cambridge Tripos. He subsequently
came to be regarded as one of the most learned men in Sri Lanka. He
succeeded Fr. Matthews as Rector in 1921, but Divine Providence deemed
otherwise and on January 20th 1924 he was raised to the purple as
the New Bishop.
Rev. Fr. Timothy M. F. Long, OMI (1936 – 1954)

In 1936, the ‘Grand Golden Era’ of the College started with
a magical word FR. LONG. Fr. Timothy
M.F. Long OMI succeeded Fr. Matthews as Rector and was at the helm till
1954. Under his guidance the College
rose to a height of glory academically as well as in sports and in almost every
sphere of educational and social development. He was imbued with ideal aims and aspirations of superlative
magnitude. He was a man of immense
faith. In his administration, he gave
priority to the religious ideals and atmosphere of the College. His selfless service during this period was
an important chapter in the history of the College. The Matthews Block will be a constant
reminder of his hard work. In 1990 the
Government of Sri Lanka recognized him as a ‘National Hero’ and issued a stamp,
enshrining the memory of his contribution to the society at large.

His faith in God, strict discipline, kind personality and
enthusiasm for higher education were what St. Patrick’s stands for today. In 1961 on the 30th of April, he
passed away to enjoy Eternal Glory.
Rev. Fr. S. N. Arulnesan, OMI (1954 – 1960)

When Sri Lanka, India and many other Asian countries
achieved political freedom and independence, the Catholic Church decided that
it was time for a native son to be made the Head of St. Patrick’s College and
appointed Fr. S. N. Arulnesan, the right person at the right place at the right
time. He has been described as
forerunner of a new age. At this time
there were many changes in the sphere of education in Sri Lanka. Swabhasha came to its own when the medium of
instruction changed from English to Tamil. Fr. Arulnesan introduced an education based on Eastern ideals and
culture. He was quiet, pleasant and
affable to associate with. He was a
person who responded to the needs and sufferings of the poor and the
lowly. His contribution to the College
shall forever be enshrined in our hearts.
Rev. Fr. P. J. Jeevaratnam, OMI (1960 – 1966)

In 1960, when Fr. S.N. Arulnesan OMI left St. Patrick’s
College, Fr. P.J. Jeevaratnam, who had been earlier the Rector of St. Henry’s
Ilavalai and of St. Antony’s Kayts, assumed charge and was Rector till
1966. He had to face all the problems
that arose, when St. Patrick’s opted to become a Private Non-Fee-Levying school
in 1961. He had to find the financial
resources t run the College. His rich
experience and mature judgement were the very qualities needed at that
challenging period in the history of the College. Fr. Jeevaratnam spent seven years of his life
in this institution and generations of students owe him a debt of
gratitude. He died on 14th
March 1975.
Rev. Fr. T. A. J. Mathuranayagam, (1966 – 1976)

In the early years of his career, Fr. Mathuram spent himself
as Teacher, Warden, Prefect of Students and Gen. Manager of the College. In everything he set an example of dedicated
labour and inspiration for generations of patricians. He had been also the Rector of St. Joseph’s
College. Anuradhapura for several years. In order to foster greater interest and involvement of the students in College
activities, he introduced the celebration of St. Patrick’s Day with the novelty
of classroom breakfast. The “LONG
INSTITUTE OF TECHNO – ENGINEERING” which was started by him proved his much
interest and concern in the welfare of the youth.For many years the foot-ball teams of St.
Patrick’s maintained an invincible records because of the encouragement and
incentive given by Fr. Mathuram. In his
period, the 125th Anniversary of the College was celebrated with
great fervor and vigour. He led the
College to great heights, true to the traditions of his predecessors and he
left a rich heritage.
Rev. Fr. John A. Francis, OMI (1976 – 1979)

Fr. John A. Francis took over the reins at a very critical
time of the school’s history. He had to
shoulder the great responsibility of the school, after the demise of Bishop
Emilianus Pillai, which St. Patrick’s remaining the only Catholic school in
Jaffna opting to continue private. Owing
to his skill and faith in God, he overcame the difficulties. Fr. John Francis was a man of deep faith and
his spirituality permeated not only the entire structure of the College but
also the Jaffna peninsula.St. Patrick’s
will gratefully treasure the dedicated and selfless service rendered by Fr.
John A. Francis, OMI.
Rev. Fr. G. A. Francis Joseph (1979 – 1992)

There is no doubt that Fr. G.A. Francis Joseph is a very
important personality in the life of St. Patrick’s College. He was appointed as Rector in 1980. He served with zealous dedication till he
retired in June 1992. Under his direction, the College became more
systematized. Rules and regulations were
framed, discipline more strictly enforced and a more all-round education was
envisaged. It is, but appropriate that
he is called the “Architect of Modern St. Patrick’s”. Old buildings were re-structured, new ones
erected and the college ground was re-laid. The construction of an upstairs block for the Primary Department, a
beautiful Mathuram Square-open air stage, a fine staffroom, science lab,
stadium and score board were some of his notable structures.

He was an understanding and sympathetic friend and guide to
the teachers. His birthdays were
special, not only for him but were celebrated by the Patrician Family as
“FAMILY DAY” to remember with gratitude the 25 years of dedicated service of
the staff. Also he organized the
“Wednesday Tea” to the staff to sit and chat together as one family, which is
even now continued in the College. He
stated the College Diary to remind the agenda of the year in advance.

He was a man whose quiet and unassuming devotion to work
revealed a variety of talent and skill. He was an excellent musician and gifted as he was with a good
voice. Being a many-sided personality,
he had agile alertness, meticulous devotion to details and constrictive
ideas. Hence every activity of the
College received his golden touch.

Rev. Fr. A.
I Bernard (1992 – 2002)

Fr. A.I.
Bernard succeeded Fr. G.A. Francis Joseph. He was a strong administrator and strict disciplinarian. He had the unique ability to bring out the
best in everyone, be it student or teacher. He devoted considerable amount of time to the encouragement of
co-curricular activities in order to develop the whole personality of each
child. The Primary Section of the
College occupied a special place in his heart. He introduced many innovations to the Primary Department both musical
and academic. The percussion band is one
of his special contribution to the tiny tots.

When war
clouds hung over the horizon in the Jaffna peninsula he had with all the tact
in his command maneuvered the school. During the mass displacement which occurred in 1995, the College had to
function in Varany. He guided this
institution under trying circumstances. When displaced people returned to Jaffna he, in the midst of political
disturbances, acted bravely confronting many challenges. The full scale of his contribution and deft
handling of these difficult matters cannot be fully measured until history had
made a perspective in due course.

Rev. Fr.
Justin B. Gnanapragasam (2002 – 2007)

The Rector’s
Report of the College Prize Day 2016 highlights Rev. Fr. Justin B.
Gnanapragasam as follows: “We are delighted that the person who had been the
helmsman of St. Patrick’s has been chosen as the Chief Pastor of the Diocese of
Jaffna.

In 1974 Rev.
Fr. Justin was ordained a Priest. He
served in Killinochchi and Valaipaadu missions and in 1976 appointed to St.
Henry’s College, Ilavalai as Vice Rector and later took over as Rector. During the period 1992 – 1996 when a mass
exodus took place in the North, he guided the destiny of St. Henry’s College
and safeguarded its glory and tradition unhindered. In 2002, he became the Rector of St.
Patrick’s College and gave himself fully for its rapid growth and
development. Fr. Justin, with his vibrant
personality and convincing approach, won the hearts of many and let them commit
and contribute generously towards his projects that enabled him to achieve many
goals. It was a time of re-emergence of
St. Patrick’s after three decades of war. Rev. Fr. Justin B. Gnanapragasam is second in line of illustrious
Rectors of St. Patrick’s after late Rev. Fr. J.A. Guyomar, OMI to be elevated
as Bishop to the See of Jaffna. Succeeding as Bishop of Jaffna, St. Patrick’s College is privileged to
have him as its Patron and Manager.

Rev. Fr. M.
Jero Selvanayagam (2007 – 2018)

Rev. Fr. M.
Jero Selvanayagam joined St. Patrick’s in 1989.He was appointed as Prefect of Studies and later hostel warden. He was a very hard and efficient worker with
wide experience in the fields of both education and sports. In 1998, he was appointed as the Vice Rector
of the College.He obtained his Master’s
Degree in Education Management from the University of London.He taught English, Religion, History and
Logic. After 10 years of very fruitful
and marvelous work as Vice Rector, he became the Rector of the College in 2008
succeeding Rev. Fr. Justin B. Gnanapragasam.

As a tactful
leader he welcomed new ideas and was open to suggestions from his team of
teachers.He was a silent observer of
men, matters and things around. His
qualities of being straight forward, gentle in dealing with people, patience
and perseverance made him popular among teachers and pupils alike.During his time, the Primary Department
received a beautiful three storey building; a pavilion was erected at the
College playground and more than 75% of the construction of the Technology
Centre had been completed.As Rector of the College, he introduced many
innovative ideas and activities in teaching and learning and was admired for
great task.No can easily forget Fr.
Jero’s nearly 30 years of self-sacrificing life and service at St. Patrick’s as
teacher, prefect of studies, warden, Vice Rector and Rector.
